purpose: Distinguish the historical act that assigned a continuity identifier from later mentions, summaries, filenames, and semantic matches.
durable_memory: A continuity identifier is historically assigned only by an immutable source object whose content explicitly performs the assignment, identifies the governed object, and predates dependent references.
assignment_authority_sources: decision log entry explicitly assigning the identifier
language lexicon entry explicitly binding the identifier
project document explicitly creating the identifier and governed object
privacy-safe chat-history evidence explicitly performing the assignment
lead_only_sources: derived graph nodes without an assignment locator

classifications.resolved: All gates pass and the assignment source is immutable.
classifications.rejected_collision: At least one identity gate demonstrably fails.
classifications.lead_only: The source mentions or resembles the identifier but does not perform the assignment.
classifications.unresolved: One or more gates remain unknown or coverage is incomplete.
classifications.unlocated_after_exhaustive_coverage: Exhaustive accessible coverage is evidenced and no assignment source is found; reconstruction remains prohibited.

observed: M-004, M-005, and M-006 remain unresolved in the active queue.
No verified originating assignment locator has been established.
inferred: Treating a reference as an assignment would create false historical certainty.
proposed: Apply this contract to every candidate found during exhaustive repository and privacy-safe source traversal.
superseded: A matching filename, suffix, semantic role, or completion summary can independently establish identifier provenance.
unresolved: The originating assignment objects for M-004, M-005, and M-006.
Whether inaccessible or unindexed history contains stronger evidence.

privacy_boundary: Retain only source class, immutable locator or digest, timestamp, gate outcomes, and classification; do not reproduce private source text.
reversibility: Revert the adding commit; no existing queue, registry, runtime, or history is modified.
